name: Voxel Art
visualIdentity: Explicitly identified as voxel art, distinct from pixel art: figures and spaces are built from consistently sized cubes, with stepped contours, controlled lighting, and color blocks for depth. Pixel texture on an arbitrary mesh does not qualify.
suitableUses: Block-built characters and worlds suit game tours, system overviews, and infrastructure explainers. Isometric framing or countable voxel units can support diagrams and verified quantity comparisons. These are inferred fits; the source directly recommends voxel worlds and those two hybrids.
limitations: Maintain one voxel size. Avoid perspective shrinkage, free camera spin, and non-voxel meshes with pixel textures. Isometric projection needs parallel edges and constrained movement. For data, each voxel must represent one stated unit, scales start at zero, and values must be verified. Motion patterns requiring facial layers, unseen sides, or real depth need suitable assets or geometry.
palette: Optional suggestion for new artwork only: background #EEE9DB, foreground #30444C, accent 1 #63928D, accent 2 #C0845D; four discrete tokens, no gradient. Supplied exact, brand, approved, or existing semantic colors take precedence and must not be recolored or expanded. Accents are decorative; foreground on background has 8.418 contrast, while accent text pairs miss the 4.5 target. Verify actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Animate complete forms or purposeful block assembly while preserving scale; transforms must derive from shared seekable time for video. Interactive HTML may add constrained button or arrow-key 90° isometric rotations, accessible data tables, and aria-live values. Optional depth parallax needs real geometry or labeled 2.5D; avoid broken contact, occlusion, projection, or labels. Scroll chapters and bounded camera moves are possible only when supported by the scene. Reduced-motion stills and reversible states suit interactive use.
audio: Unspecified: no fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required layer. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied requirements and assets. Synchronize and mix with picture, preserve speech clarity, avoid clipping, and review them together.
assetRequirements: Build cube instances of consistent dimensions; track block color and visibility and compute assembly transforms from time. Three.js with InstancedMesh is recommended for efficient repeated cubes. Prepare suitable geometry, labels, and verified source data for hybrids. Load local fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not imply simulated appearance is physical production.
combinations: Use alone for block-built worlds. With orthographic isometric diagrams, keep parallel edges and one voxel size; suggested HTML controls rotate in 90° steps, with labels and a reduced-motion still. With unit-based data, one voxel equals one verified unit, use teal and terracotta categories, zero-based scales, accessible table and value announcements; never invent data or use decorative block explosions.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method for visual fidelity first; Three.js/InstancedMesh owns voxel geometry and lighting, and a suitable timeline owns motion. HyperFrames is the default for composition, seekable timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. Do not mix frameworks or let pipeline defaults replace rendering or motion. Use deterministic composition time; inspect key frames and full decoded video, including dimensions, duration, frame rate, sync, and loop continuity. Audio and exact output specs are task-dependent or unspecified.
